fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is pre-oxidation, whereas the target intervention is changing ambient temperature during nanoindentation and friction simulations.

Oxide-layer formation is not part of the target system or mechanism; the target attributes degradation above approximately 900 K to lattice disorder, dislocation-density reduction, and a transition away from stacking-fault-mediated deformation.
The cited evidence does not directly establish protective pre-oxidation in FeNiCrCoCu coatings on Cu; the strongest wear evidence concerns a compositionally and structurally different bulk HEA.
The predicted improvement in high-temperature wear resistance does not reconstruct the target result of sharply decreasing hardness and wear resistance near and above 900 K.
explanation: This is a clear and experimentally falsifiable alternative hypothesis, but it is not a reconstruction of the target study. It introduces an oxygen atmosphere and pre-oxidation treatment absent from the target molecular-dynamics system, omits the specified FeNiCrCoCu/Cu geometry and indentation protocol, and proposes an oxide-barrier mechanism instead of temperature-driven lattice disorder and dislocation evolution. Its threshold of 600°C (873 K) is numerically close to the target transition near 900 K, but the physical rationale and predicted trend differ. E3 provides useful precedent that tribo-oxides can improve elevated-temperature wear in another HEA, while E1 supports Cr-related oxidation resistance more generally; neither validates a continuous protective Cu/Cr-rich oxide or dislocation suppression in this exact coating. The paired-coating experiment and measurements are discriminating, although oxide adhesion and spallation should also be measured.
